_meta.description: The shipped SoD ruleset. Extracted from modules/access_risk_analysis.py so that the people who know SAP best can review and correct it without editing Python - the same reason data/finding_details.json was extracted.
_meta.provenance_note: Every rule carries its own `provenance` field naming the tier its authorization objects came from. Only the original finance rules were verified object by object; the rest were written from general SAP knowledge, and SODCOV-007 measures them against a system's own TOBJ catalogue when one is supplied.
_meta.editing: A rule needs risk_id, risk_type, and a `functions` list. A SOD rule needs two functions; a CRITICAL_ACTION or CRITICAL_PERMISSION rule needs one. Every function needs actions, permissions, or both - a function with neither is held by every user. Every permission needs an object. tests/test_shipped_ruleset.py enforces all of this.

risks.name: Maintain Vendor Master and Process Vendor Payment
risks.rationale: A user who can create/change the vendor master AND execute outgoing payments can set up a ghost vendor and pay it, or redirect a real vendor's payment. Canonical AP fraud path. Maintain (ACTVT 01/02) on vendor combined with execute (not display) on payment must fire.
references: SAP GRC Access Control default ruleset (Maintain Vendor / Process Payment)

risks.name: Maintain Vendor Bank Details and Run Automatic Payment Program
risks.rationale: Highest-value refinement of P2P-01: the same user changes the vendor bank account (IBAN/bank key) and runs F110 that pays it, routing funds to an attacker account with no second pair of eyes. Bank-detail change governed by sensitive-field object F_LFA1_AEN.
references: SAP GRC / Pathlock P2P ruleset (Maintain Vendor Bank vs Run Payment)

risks.name: Create/Change Purchase Order and Release Purchase Order
risks.rationale: A user who raises/changes a PO and releases (approves) it defeats the purchasing approval control, enabling self-authorized spend. Release authority = holding a release code in M_EINK_FRG (no ACTVT field).
references: SAP GRC default ruleset (PO Create vs PO Release)

risks.name: Create Purchase Order and Post Goods Receipt
risks.rationale: A user who creates a PO and posts the goods receipt against it can confirm receipt of goods never delivered, driving the three-way match to auto-approve a fraudulent invoice.
references: SAP GRC default ruleset (PO Create vs Goods Receipt)

risks.name: Create Purchase Order and Post Vendor Invoice (MIRO)
risks.rationale: A user who creates a PO and posts the logistics invoice (MIRO) originates both the commitment and the payable, manipulating qty/price to overpay a colluding/fictitious vendor. Breaks the three-way match.
references: SAP GRC default ruleset (PO Create vs Invoice Processing)

risks.name: Maintain Vendor Master and Post AP (Non-PO) Vendor Invoice
risks.rationale: A user who creates/changes vendors and posts AP invoices can create a fictitious vendor and book a non-PO (FI) invoice against it, generating an open payable a later payment run settles. Covers the FB60/F-43 path MIRO risks do not.
references: SAP GRC default ruleset (Maintain Vendor vs Post AP Invoice)

risks.name: Maintain Customer Master and Create Sales Order
risks.rationale: A user who creates/changes customer master AND creates sales orders can set up a fictitious/altered customer and immediately book sales/deliveries to it, enabling diverted goods or fraudulent revenue with no independent check on the counterparty.

risks.name: Maintain Customer Credit Limit and Release Credit-Blocked Sales Order
risks.rationale: A user who maintains credit limits/risk category AND releases credit-blocked SD documents defeats credit control: raise a limit or release regardless, pushing through orders that should be blocked and concealing over-exposure.

risks.name: Post/Clear Incoming Customer Payments and Maintain Customer Master
risks.rationale: Classic cash-misappropriation/lapping conflict: a user who applies/clears incoming customer payments AND maintains the customer master can divert a payment then cover the shortfall by altering the account, resetting cleared items (FBRA), or writing it off.
references: SAP GRC default ruleset (Process Customer Payments & Maintain Customer)

risks.name: Maintain Pricing/Condition Records and Create Sales Order
risks.rationale: A user who maintains pricing/condition records AND creates sales orders can grant unauthorized prices/discounts and consume them on their own orders — kickbacks, under-billing of favored customers, margin erosion.
references: SAP GRC default ruleset O2C Pricing

risks.name: Post Billing Document and Maintain Customer Master
risks.rationale: A user who posts billing documents AND maintains the customer master can invoice/credit-memo a customer whose terms, bank data, or existence they control — fabricated invoices/credit memos routed to an account they set up.
references: SAP GRC default ruleset O2C Billing

risks.name: Create Sales Order and Release Own Credit-Blocked Order
risks.rationale: A sales user who creates orders AND releases credit-blocked SD documents self-approves their own credit blocks: any order tripping the credit check can be released by the same person, nullifying the credit safeguard through delivery and billing.
references: SAP GRC default ruleset O2C Create Order & Release

risks.name: Maintain G/L Account Master Data and Post Journal Entries
risks.rationale: A user who creates/changes G/L account master AND posts accounting documents can set up a fictitious/suspense account and post fraudulent or concealing journals to it. Classic financial-statement-fraud and misappropriation-concealment SoD.

functions.name: Post Journal Entry / Manual G/L Posting

risks.name: Maintain G/L Account Master Data and Open/Close Posting Periods
risks.rationale: A user who maintains G/L master AND opens/closes posting periods (OB52) can create/alter accounts and reopen a closed period to back-date entries into them, defeating period-end cutoff and master-data governance.

risks.name: Enter/Park and Post Journal Entries (four-eyes bypass)
risks.rationale: Parking splits preparation (park/enter) from approval (post). A user who can both park/enter and post/release parked documents defeats the four-eyes control on manual JE — a key SOX control. Park=ACTVT 77, post=ACTVT 01; distinguish park-only from post.

functions.name: Post Journal Entry / Post Parked Document

risks.name: Maintain Exchange Rates and Post Journal Entries
risks.rationale: A user who maintains exchange rates (OB08/TCURR) AND posts accounting documents can manipulate the FX rate used on a foreign-currency posting/revaluation to book fictitious gains, understate liabilities, or shift value between entities, then post — with no independent rate control.

functions.name: Post Journal Entry / Manual G/L Posting

risks.name: Open/Close Posting Periods and Post Journal Entries
risks.rationale: A user who opens/closes posting periods (OB52) AND posts accounting documents can reopen a closed period to back-date, or push entries into a still-open period, then post unauthorized journals — defeating period-end cutoff and month-end close.

functions.name: Post Journal Entry / Manual G/L Posting

risks.name: Maintain HR Master Data and Execute Payroll Run
risks.rationale: A user who changes pay-relevant master data (Basic Pay IT0008, Recurring Payments/Deductions IT0014, Additional Payments IT0015) AND executes the payroll driver can inflate their own or an accomplice's pay and process it into a live payroll result with no review. Flagship H2R SoD.

risks.name: Maintain Employee Bank Details and Run Payroll / Generate Payments
risks.rationale: A user who changes Bank Details (IT0009) AND runs payroll or creates the payment medium/DME file can redirect net pay to an attacker account and push the payment out in the same period. Classic payroll-diversion fraud.

risks.name: Maintain Personnel Actions (Hire/Terminate) and Maintain Time Data
risks.rationale: A user who runs personnel actions (hire/rehire/terminate via PA40, creating IT0000/0001/0002/0008) AND enters time data (IT2xxx via PA61/PA62) can create a ghost employee and book the hours that generate pay for it.

risks.name: Execute Payroll Run and Post Payroll Results to Accounting
risks.rationale: Separating who runs/simulates payroll from who creates and posts the posting run to FI is a standard payroll control. A user holding both can push fraudulent or unreviewed payroll results straight into the GL with no four-eyes check between calculation and posting.

risks.name: User Administration vs Authorization/Profile Administration
risks.rationale: A single user who administers user master records (create users, reset passwords, assign roles/profiles) AND defines what roles/profiles grant (build authorizations) can grant themselves unlimited access with no four-eyes control. Foundational Basis privilege-escalation SoD.

functions.name: User Administration (create/change users, assign roles & profiles)

risks.name: Maintain Role vs Assign Role to User
risks.rationale: The person who BUILDS a role (its transactions and authorization values) must not be the person who ASSIGNS it to users. Combined, a user could insert powerful access into a role and assign it to their own account, bypassing role-owner approval. Build-vs-assign split at role granularity.

functions.name: Maintain Role Content (build role menu & authorizations)

risks.name: ABAP Development vs Transport Release/Import to Production
risks.rationale: A developer who writes/changes ABAP AND releases their own transports and imports them into production defeats change-management four-eyes control, moving untested or malicious code (backdoors) into PRD unreviewed.

functions.name: Release & Import Transport Requests to Production

risks.name: Maintain Table Data vs Administer Security Audit Log
risks.rationale: A user who directly changes sensitive table contents AND configures/deactivates the logging that records those changes (Security Audit Log via SM19/RSAU_CONFIG) can make and then conceal fraudulent changes. Separating data maintenance from audit administration preserves an untampered trail.

functions.name: Administer Security Audit Log / Change Logging

references: SAP Help Configuring the Security Audit Log (SM19/RSAU_CONFIG)

risks.name: Maintain Purchasing Info Record and Create Purchase Order
risks.rationale: The info record carries the price the purchase order defaults to. A user who can set the price and then raise the order against it fixes what the company pays without a second pair of eyes, and the order looks entirely ordinary because the price it used is the one on file.
references: SAP Help MM Purchasing: M_EINF_EKG / M_EINF_EKO (purchasing info record)
SAP Help MM Purchasing: M_BEST_BSA / M_BEST_EKO

risks.name: Create Purchase Requisition and Release It
risks.rationale: The requisition release strategy is the first approval in the procurement chain. Raising the demand and approving it are the same person's actions here, so the release step records an approval that never happened independently and every downstream control inherits an unapproved requirement.
references: SAP Help MM Purchasing: M_BANF_BSA / M_BANF_EKG (requisition)
SAP Help MM Purchasing: M_EINK_FRG (release code)

risks.name: Post Goods Receipt and Post Vendor Invoice
risks.rationale: Three-way match is the control: someone orders, someone confirms receipt, someone verifies the invoice. A user holding the receipt and the invoice confirms goods that never arrived and then pays for them, and the match succeeds because both sides of it were entered by the same person.
references: SAP Help MM: M_MSEG_BWA / M_MSEG_WWE (goods movement)
SAP Help MM: M_RECH_BUK / M_RECH_WRK (invoice verification)

risks.name: Release Blocked Invoice and Execute Vendor Payment
risks.rationale: An invoice is blocked because something failed the match - price, quantity or date. Releasing that block and then running the payment removes the only control standing between a disputed invoice and the money leaving, and the release leaves a record showing the discrepancy was reviewed.
references: SAP Help FI: F_REGU_BUK (automatic payment, FBTCH)

risks.name: Maintain Material Master Valuation and Post Goods Movement
risks.rationale: The material master's accounting view carries the valuation price against which every goods movement posts. Changing the price and then moving the stock writes an inventory value the person choosing it also decided, which is how inventory shrinkage is concealed as a revaluation.
references: SAP Help MM: M_MATE_BUK / M_MATE_MAT (material master)

risks.name: Create Sales Order and Post Goods Issue
risks.rationale: Raising the order and issuing the goods against it moves inventory out of the business on one person's authority. Where the customer is fictitious or the order is later cancelled, the stock has already gone and the only record of why is the document its creator wrote.
references: SAP Help SD: V_VBAK_AAT / V_VBAK_VKO (sales document)
SAP Help SD: V_LIKP_VST (delivery, shipping point)

risks.name: Create Credit Memo Request and Bill It
risks.rationale: A credit memo returns money or cancels a receivable. Raising the request and converting it to a billing document is the sales-side equivalent of writing a cheque to oneself, and it is the standard route by which a receivable owed by a colluding customer quietly disappears.
references: SAP Help SD: V_VBAK_AAT (sales document type)

risks.name: Maintain Customer Master and Execute Dunning
risks.rationale: Dunning is the control that surfaces overdue receivables. A user who can set a customer's dunning block or level and then run the dunning programme decides which debts are chased, so a receivable from a related party can be kept permanently invisible without any write-off appearing.
references: SAP Help FI: F_KNA1_BUK / F_KNA1_APP (customer master)
SAP Help FI: F_MAHN_BUK (dunning, company code)

risks.name: Maintain Asset Master and Post Asset Acquisition or Retirement
risks.rationale: Creating the asset and posting its acquisition or retirement puts the whole fixed-asset lifecycle in one pair of hands. A retirement posted against an asset the same person created removes a book value with no independent confirmation the asset ever existed or has genuinely gone.
references: SAP Help FI-AA: A_S_ANLKL (asset master, company code / asset class)
SAP Help FI: F_BKPF_BUK (accounting document, company code)

risks.name: Maintain House Bank / Bank Master and Execute Payment Run
risks.rationale: The house bank and bank master decide which account money leaves from and which it arrives at. Changing them and then running the payment programme is the treasury equivalent of P2P-02: the destination and the disbursement are chosen by one person, and the payment file itself looks correct.
references: SAP Help FI: F_BNKA_MAN (bank master data)
SAP Help FI: F_REGU_BUK (automatic payment transactions)

risks.name: Maintain Recurring Entry and Execute the Recurring Run
risks.rationale: A recurring entry posts on a schedule with no further human step. Defining the template and running it means a journal posts every period on the authority of the person who wrote it, and because the postings are routine they attract none of the scrutiny a one-off entry of the same value would.
references: SAP Help FI: F_BKPF_BUK (accounting document, company code)
SAP Help: S_BDC_MONI (batch input session monitoring)

risks.name: Open the Client and Import a Transport
risks.rationale: Transport-only change is the control the whole ITGC framework rests on. A user who can both open the production client and import transports can introduce a change by either route and close the door behind them, so the system's own settings will later assert that only transports arrived.

risks.name: Maintain Authorization Check Indicators and Build Roles
risks.rationale: SU24 decides which authorization objects PFCG proposes for a transaction, and a check indicator set to 'no check' removes an object from every role built afterwards while the transaction still works. A user who can edit SU24 and build roles can therefore create a role that passes permission-level review because the object the review looks for is no longer proposed.
references: SAP Help: SU24 maintains USOBT_C / USOBX_C; only customer defaults are applied by PFCG

risks.name: Generic Table Maintenance (SE16/SM30 write access)
risks.rationale: A user who can change table contents directly through the Data Browser or table maintenance performs the DATA half of every business conflict without holding any business transaction. Changing LFA1/LFBK is 'maintain vendor' with no FK02; changing BSEG is 'post document' with no FB01. SAP's own EarlyWatch Alert lists users who can change all tables as a critical finding, and Note 1541577 exists precisely because S_TABU_NAM breaks rulesets keyed on S_TABU_DIS. This is the single most common way a transaction-level SoD report reads clean over a compromised estate.
references: SAP EarlyWatch Alert - Security (ABAP): Users Authorized to Change or Display all Tables
SAP Help: S_TABU_DIS (DICBERCLS, ACTVT); S_TABU_NAM (TABLE, ACTVT)
SAP Note 1541577 - Impact of S_TABU_NAM in Risk Analysis and Remediation

risks.name: Debug and Replace in Production (S_DEVELOP DEBUG ACTVT 02)
risks.rationale: Debug-replace edits variable values in a running program, which means it alters the result of an AUTHORITY-CHECK AFTER the check has executed. No authorization object, organisational level or SoD rule can constrain a user who holds it: the canonical /h + change sy-subrc technique defeats every control this ruleset expresses. SAP's Security Optimization Guide names S_DEVELOP in production as critical on its own.

functions.name: Change Variables in the ABAP Debugger

references: SAP Help: Rights for Debugging - S_DEVELOP OBJTYPE DEBUG, ACTVT 02 allows editing values of variables in the ABAP debugger
SAP Security Optimization Guide: Protecting ABAP Development Environment
SAP EarlyWatch Alert - Security: Users Authorized to Debug / Replace

risks.name: Execute Any ABAP Report (SA38/SE38 with unrestricted S_PROGRAM)
risks.rationale: Running an arbitrary report bypasses the transaction code the ruleset keys on. The program behind a transaction can be submitted directly, so a user with SA38 reaches the capability without ever holding the transaction - the false-negative direction, and the more dangerous of the two. SAP's EarlyWatch Alert reports users authorized to start all reports as a distinct critical finding.
references: SAP EarlyWatch Alert - Security (ABAP): Users Authorized to Start all Reports

risks.name: Schedule a Background Job Step Under Another User
risks.rationale: By default a job runs under the authorizations of the user who scheduled it. S_BTCH_NAM lifts that: the step runs as a named other user, so a clerk holding only FB60 can schedule a step that executes F110 as a batch account. The two halves of a real conflict then sit in two identities and USER-LEVEL SoD analysis reports nothing, while one human executed both. SAP restricts this authorization to the batch administrator for exactly this reason.

functions.name: Run a Job Step as Another User

references: SAP Help: Defining Users for Background Processing - 'You should give this authorization to the batch administrator only'
SAP Help: Authorizations for Background Processing - a job runs under the authorizations of the user who scheduled it

risks.name: Administer RFC Destinations (SM59)
risks.rationale: An RFC destination holding stored credentials is a privilege capsule: the caller needs only S_RFC for the function group and then executes in the target system as the stored user, frequently a wide-authorization service account. Whoever can create or edit destinations can therefore manufacture a path into any connected system, and none of it appears in their own role portfolio. SAP's EarlyWatch Alert lists RFC administrators as a critical group.
references: SAP EarlyWatch Alert - Security (ABAP): Users Authorized to Administer RFC Connections

risks.name: Trusted-RFC Logon Without a Password (S_RFCACL)
risks.rationale: S_RFCACL lets a caller assume an identity in the target system with no password, the calling system asserting who they are. SAP deliberately excludes it from SAP_ALL - one of very few objects it withholds - and warns that individual users might be misused as anonymous users to perform actions in the target system. A holder inherits whatever the asserted identity can do, in a system where no SoD analysis of the source estate can see it.
references: SAP RFC/ICF Security Guide: 'The object S_RFCACL is not included in the authorization profile SAP_ALL'; 'individual users might be misused as anonymous users to perform actions in the target system'
SAP Help: as of Release 40B SAP_ALL does not contain an authorization for S_RFCACL

risks.name: Cross-Client Table Maintenance (S_TABU_CLI)
risks.rationale: Cross-client tables are shared by every client on the system, so a change made from a sandbox or training client takes effect in production on the same instance. Client separation is the control most estates rely on to make a non-production client harmless; this authorization removes it, and it does so without appearing in any business transaction.
references: SAP Help: S_TABU_CLI (CLIIDMAINT) - cross-client table maintenance

risks.name: Execute External Operating-System Commands (SM49/SM69)
risks.rationale: An external command runs on the application server under the SAP system's operating-system account. Whoever can define or execute one steps outside the ABAP authorization concept entirely - reading or replacing files, invoking database utilities, or launching a shell - so no SoD rule, org level or table protection constrains what follows. Defining the command and executing it are separately protected for that reason.

functions.name: Define or Execute External OS Commands

references: SAP Help: S_LOG_COM (COMMAND, OPSYSTEM, HOST) - external operating system commands
SAP Help: S_RZL_ADM - CCMS system administration

risks.name: Application-Server File Access from ABAP (S_DATASET)
risks.rationale: S_DATASET governs OPEN DATASET, so a holder reads and writes files on the application server: payment files awaiting transmission to the bank, interface drops, and transport data. A payment file altered after approval and before transmission changes the payee with no document, no change record and no transaction anywhere in an SoD ruleset.

functions.name: Read or Write Server Files from ABAP

references: SAP Help: S_DATASET (PROGRAM, ACTVT, FILENAME) - authorization for file access

risks.name: Open the Production Client for Changes (SCC4)
risks.rationale: Client settings decide whether production accepts direct configuration change and cross-client customizing. A user who can open the client removes the control that makes 'changes only arrive by transport' true, and can then make a change directly, close the client again, and leave a system whose settings say it was never open. Every downstream control that assumes transport-only change inherits the failure.
references: SAP Help: client maintenance (SCC4), table T000
SAP Help: S_TABU_CLI for cross-client maintenance

risks.name: Change Payroll Status / Delete Payroll Results
risks.rationale: PU03 edits the Payroll Status infotype (IT0003) — unlock a personnel number, reset accounted-to/earliest-retro date and correction flags — while PU01 deletes the current payroll result. Together they re-open a closed/locked period, wipe a result and recalculate, defeating payroll locking and enabling undetected manipulation.

risks.name: Maintain Own HR Master Data (P_PERNR PSIGN=I)
risks.rationale: P_PERNR (Personnel Number Check) with PSIGN='I' (own personnel number) at write level lets a user maintain their OWN pay-relevant infotypes (Basic Pay 0008, Bank Details 0009) — self-service pay manipulation. When the PERNR main switch is active (OOAC, AUTSW/PERNR), P_PERNR overrides P_ORGIN; PSIGN='I' with write AUTHC is the exact self-maintenance grant. Best practice PSIGN='E' (exclude own record) for pay-relevant infotypes.
references: SAP Help P_PERNR PSIGN I/E, main switch OOAC (AUTSW/PERNR)

risks.name: Maintain BOM / Routing and Release Production Order
risks.provenance: objects from design spec (C_STUE_BER, C_ROUT, C_AFKO_AWK); fields unverified
risks.rationale: A user who changes what a product is made of (BOM) or how it is made (routing) AND releases the production order that consumes it can quietly alter component quantities, then run the order that draws the extra material — the consumption becomes 'planned' and reconciles cleanly. Costing is distorted in the same motion. Authorization-based on both sides.
references: S/4HANA security design specification — PP authorization objects
SAP GRC starter ruleset — Manufacturing (BOM/routing vs order release)

risks.name: Confirm Production Order and Post Component Goods Movement
risks.provenance: objects from design spec (C_AFKO_AWK, M_MSEG_BWA/WMB); fields unverified
risks.rationale: Confirmation declares the yield and scrap a production order achieved; the goods movement books the components it consumed and the finished stock it produced. One user holding both can confirm output that was never made, or write off good material as scrap and remove it — the classic false-production-confirmation loss, invisible because the paperwork agrees with itself.
references: S/4HANA security design specification — PP / Inventory objects
SAP GRC starter ruleset — Manufacturing (confirm vs component GI/GR)

risks.name: Post Goods Movement and Post Physical Inventory Difference
risks.provenance: objects from design spec (M_MSEG_BWA/WMB); fields unverified
risks.rationale: The count is the control that catches the theft. A user who moves stock AND posts the physical-inventory difference writes off exactly what they removed — the book balance is corrected to match the shelf, the variance is 'explained', and no reconciliation ever surfaces it. Posting an inventory difference is itself a material movement (types 701/702), so the movement-type authorization governs both sides.
references: S/4HANA security design specification — Inventory objects and MI07 flow
SAP GRC starter ruleset — Inventory (goods movement vs inventory difference)

risks.name: Post Goods Movement and Maintain Material Valuation / Status
risks.provenance: objects from design spec (M_MSEG_BWA, M_MATE_MAR/STA); fields unverified
risks.rationale: A user who moves stock AND maintains the material master can change the valuation class, price control or material status that governs how the movement is valued and whether it is blocked — writing stock off at a price they chose, or unblocking a material to move it and re-blocking it afterwards. The master data decides what the movement means.
references: S/4HANA security design specification — Material master objects
SAP GRC starter ruleset — Inventory / material master

risks.name: Record Inspection Results and Make the Usage Decision
risks.provenance: objects from design spec (Q_INSP_WRK); TRANSACTION-separated with a permission floor
risks.rationale: Quality assurance is two people by design: one records what the inspection measured, another decides whether the lot is acceptable. One user doing both can enter passing results and accept their own lot, releasing defective material to customers or production with no independent gate. Separated by transaction with an inspection-lot permission floor rather than by object — coarser than an authorization-based rule, and stated as such.
references: S/4HANA security design specification — QM authorization objects
SAP GRC starter ruleset — Quality (results recording vs usage decision)

risks.name: Make Usage Decision and Maintain Material QM Inspection Setup
risks.provenance: objects from design spec (Q_INSP_WRK, M_MATE_MAR/QM material); fields unverified
risks.rationale: Accepting a failing lot is a single event somebody may notice. Changing the material's QM inspection setup so future lots are not inspected at all is the same fraud made permanent, and it stops generating evidence. A user holding both can accept today's defective batch and switch off tomorrow's inspection.
references: S/4HANA security design specification — QM objects (Q_MATERIAL, Q_INSP_WRK)
SAP GRC starter ruleset — Quality (usage decision vs inspection setup)

risks.name: Create Maintenance Order and Confirm the Work
risks.provenance: objects from design spec (I_AUART, I_IWERK); I_* field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: A maintenance order authorises spend — labour, parts, external services — and the confirmation says the work happened. One user raising the order and confirming it can book maintenance that was never performed, consuming spare parts that leave the storeroom to somewhere else, or route an external service to a colluding contractor with the confirmation as the only evidence.
references: S/4HANA security design specification — PM/EAM authorization objects
SAP GRC starter ruleset — Plant Maintenance (order vs confirmation)

risks.name: Maintain Project Budget and Settle Project Costs
risks.provenance: objects from design spec (C_PRPS_ART, C_PROJ_TCD, K_ORDER); fields unverified
risks.rationale: Project budget is the control that stops a project absorbing cost without approval, and settlement is what moves that cost onto an asset or a P&L account. A user who sets the budget AND settles can raise the budget to cover an overrun they then settle away — the overrun never surfaces as a variance, and capital projects are where the largest single-approval amounts in an ERP live.
references: S/4HANA security design specification — PS authorization objects
SAP GRC starter ruleset — Project System (budget vs settlement)

risks.name: Create Warehouse Transfer Order and Confirm It
risks.provenance: objects from design spec (L_LGNUM); fields unverified
risks.rationale: The transfer order says stock should move; the confirmation says it did. A user holding both can confirm a movement that never physically happened — the bin balance in the system matches the paperwork while the goods are gone, and the discrepancy only appears at the next physical count, by which time the trail is a system record the same user created.
references: S/4HANA security design specification — WM/EWM objects (L_LGNUM)
SAP GRC starter ruleset — Warehouse (task creation vs confirmation)

risks.name: Maintain Outline Agreement and Create Release Order Against It
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: A contract or scheduling agreement fixes the price and quantity every release order draws on. A user who maintains the agreement and then orders against it sets the price they are about to pay, and each individual release looks compliant because it matches a contract nobody else reviewed.

risks.name: Create Service Entry Sheet and Accept It
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: Services leave nothing to count. The entry sheet is the only assertion that work was performed, and acceptance is the control that a second person agrees it was. One user holding both can accept their own claim that an external service happened, and the invoice that follows will reconcile against it perfectly.

risks.name: Maintain Vendor Account Group or Reconciliation Account and Post Vendor Invoice
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: The account group and reconciliation account decide which G/L the payable lands in and which fields are even visible on the vendor. Changing that and posting the invoice lets a user route a payable to an account nobody reconciles, or open a field the account group was configured to suppress.

functions.name: Maintain Vendor Account Group / Reconciliation Account

risks.name: Create Purchase Requisition and Convert It to a Purchase Order
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: The requisition is the business justification and the order is the commitment. Converting your own requisition - especially through the automatic conversion transactions, which bypass the screen a buyer would read - collapses the demand and the commitment into one decision.

risks.name: Maintain Source List or Quota Arrangement and Create Purchase Order
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: The source list decides which vendor may be used for a material and the quota arrangement decides how much each one gets. A user who maintains either and raises the order can direct spend to a chosen vendor while every individual order passes source determination cleanly.

risks.name: Maintain Customer Master and Post Customer Credit Memo
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: A credit memo reduces what a customer owes. Holding the customer master as well means the same user can create or alter the account and then write down its balance, which is how a receivable is made to disappear without cash ever arriving.

risks.name: Remove Billing Block and Create the Billing Document
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: The billing block is the hold placed on an order that should not yet be invoiced - pending approval, pending delivery, pending a price review. A user who can lift the block and raise the invoice removes the reason the hold existed and completes the transaction in the same session.

functions.name: Remove Billing / Delivery Block on Sales Document

risks.name: Create Returns Order and Receive the Returned Goods
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: A return reverses a sale: the order says goods are coming back and the receipt says they arrived. One user raising the returns order and receiving against it can credit a customer for stock that was never returned, and the two documents reconcile against each other perfectly because the same person created both. Note that posting and REVERSING a goods issue is deliberately not modelled as a segregation pair - MIGO and VL02N each perform both, so that exposure is an activity-level restriction (movement type) rather than a conflict between two duties.

risks.name: Maintain Rebate or Condition Agreement and Settle It
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: The agreement sets what the customer is owed back and the settlement pays it. One user holding both decides the rebate rate and then releases the credit against it, with no independent view of whether the accrual was ever justified.

risks.name: Maintain Customer Master and Clear or Write Off the Receivable
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: Clearing writes off what is owed. With the customer master as well, one user can set up or alter the account, run the sale through it, and then clear the balance - a complete cycle with no cash and no second pair of eyes at any point.

risks.name: Maintain Cost Centre Master and Execute Cost Allocation
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: Allocation moves cost between cost objects. A user who owns the master data and runs the allocation can move overspend off a centre that is about to be reviewed and onto one that is not, and the cycle definition they wrote is the only record of why.

functions.name: Maintain Cost Centre / Profit Centre Master

risks.name: Import Bank Statement and Clear the Resulting Open Items
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: The statement is the external evidence of what the bank actually did, and clearing is the assertion that it matches the ledger. One user doing both controls the reconciliation on both sides, which is where a missing receipt is made to look reconciled.

functions.name: Clear Open Items / Post Reconciliation Entries

risks.name: Maintain Tax Codes and Post Journal Entries
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: The tax code decides the rate and the account the tax posts to. Changing it and posting the entry lets one user book a transaction at a rate they set, and tax accounts are reconciled infrequently enough that the difference sits for a long time.

risks.name: Maintain Document Change Rules and Change a Posted Document
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: Document change rules decide which fields of a posted document may still be altered. A user who can widen those rules and then edit the document has removed the constraint that makes a posted entry final, and the change log records a permitted change.

risks.name: Maintain FI Document Number Ranges and Post Journal Entries
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: The number range is what makes a document sequence auditable. A user who can move the current number and post entries can create documents outside the expected sequence, or reuse a range, and completeness testing that relies on unbroken numbering will not see it.

risks.name: Maintain Organisational Structure and Maintain HR Master Data
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: Structural authorisation derives from the org model: who reports to whom decides whose records a manager may see. A user who edits the structure and the master data can place themselves above a population and then read or change its records, with the widened access looking like an ordinary reporting line.

risks.name: Maintain Time Data and Execute the Payroll Run
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: Time data drives what payroll pays. Entering the hours and running the calculation places both the input and the settlement in one pair of hands, and an overtime entry that is never reviewed becomes a payment that reconciles perfectly against the record supporting it.

risks.name: Maintain Wage Types or Pay Scales and Maintain HR Master Data
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: The wage type defines what a payment is and how it is treated for tax and posting; the pay scale defines the amount. A user who can create a wage type and assign it on an employee record has built and used their own payment instrument.

risks.name: Maintain Employee Master Data and Approve Travel Expenses
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: Expense approval assumes the approver is not the claimant and that bank details are somebody else's responsibility. Holding the master data as well means one user can approve a claim and direct where the reimbursement is paid.

risks.name: Maintain the Payroll Control Record and Execute Payroll
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: The control record is what opens and closes a payroll period and what prevents a closed period being rerun. A user who can move it and run payroll can reopen a settled period, recalculate it, and close it again, with the control record itself being the only evidence of the original state.

risks.name: Create Production Order and Settle It
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: The order collects the cost and the settlement decides where that cost lands. One user creating the order and settling it chooses both what was consumed and which cost object absorbs it, which is how a variance is moved off a product line before anyone reviews it.

risks.name: Maintain Work Centre or Capacity and Confirm Production
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: The work centre carries the rates that convert a confirmation into cost. Changing the rate and then confirming the operation lets one user decide both how long the work notionally took and what an hour of it is worth.

risks.name: Confirm Production Order and Reverse the Confirmation
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: Reversal is how a confirmation is undone. A user who can confirm and reverse can post consumption, draw the components, and then cancel the confirmation so that the order looks untouched while the material has already moved.

risks.name: Create Physical Inventory Document and Enter the Count
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: The count is the independent check on what the system says is there. A user who raises the inventory document and enters the count is checking their own records, and a shortage can be counted as present with no second observer at any stage.

risks.name: Maintain Batch Master and Post Goods Movement
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: The batch carries the characteristics that decide whether stock is usable and where it may go. A user who edits the batch and moves the stock can release material that a status was holding back, and the movement will look like an ordinary transfer of unrestricted stock.

risks.name: Maintain Material Master Units of Measure and Post Physical Inventory Differences
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: The unit-of-measure conversion decides how a counted quantity becomes a stock quantity. A user who can change the conversion and post the difference can make a shortage arithmetic rather than physical - the count was right, the factor was changed, and the write-off closes the gap. Note that posting and REVERSING a goods movement is deliberately not modelled as a segregation pair, because MIGO performs both: that exposure is an activity-level restriction on movement type, not a conflict between two duties.

functions.name: Maintain Material Master Units / Storage Data

risks.name: Maintain Inspection Plan and Record Inspection Results
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: The inspection plan decides what is measured and what counts as a pass. A user who writes the plan and records the results against it sets the test and marks their own paper, and a specification quietly widened will make failing material pass on the record.

risks.name: Maintain Sampling Procedure and Make the Usage Decision
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: The sampling procedure decides how much of a lot is examined before a judgement is made. Controlling that and the usage decision lets one user shrink the sample and then accept the lot, so the decision rests on evidence they chose the size of.

risks.name: Maintain Equipment or Functional Location and Create Maintenance Order
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: The technical object is what an order is raised against and what its cost settles to. A user who can create equipment and raise orders against it can book maintenance spend to an asset that exists only as a master record.

risks.name: Create Maintenance Order and Settle It
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: The order authorises the spend and the settlement decides which cost object carries it. Holding both lets one user raise maintenance work and then place its cost where it will attract least attention.

risks.name: Maintain Maintenance Plan and Confirm the Work
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: The maintenance plan generates the orders and the confirmation closes them. A user holding both can schedule work that is never done and confirm it, and the plan's own history is the evidence that the asset was maintained.

risks.name: Maintain WBS Structure and Confirm Network Activities
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: The WBS decides which element cost lands on and the confirmation says the work happened. A user who can restructure the project and confirm against it can move effort onto an element with budget left, and the structure change is indistinguishable from ordinary project replanning.

risks.name: Maintain Project Settlement Rule and Execute Settlement
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: The settlement rule decides where project cost finally goes - expense, or an asset under construction that capitalises it. Writing the rule and running the settlement lets one user choose whether spend hits this year's result at all.

risks.name: Maintain Storage Bin or Warehouse Master and Post Stock Transfer
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: The bin structure is the map of where stock is. A user who can create bins and move stock into them can park material in a location nobody counts, and the system will show the warehouse in balance.

risks.name: Confirm Transfer Order and Post Warehouse Inventory Differences
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: Confirmation asserts stock moved; the difference posting absorbs whatever does not reconcile afterwards. One user with both can confirm a movement that did not happen and then write off the resulting gap as a counting difference.

risks.name: Create Outbound Delivery and Confirm the Picking
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: The delivery says what should leave and the pick confirmation says it was taken from the bin. Holding both lets one user create a shipment and confirm it was picked, so goods leave against paperwork that had no second party at any point.

risks.name: Maintain RFC Destinations and Execute Remote Function Modules
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: An RFC destination can carry stored credentials into another system. A user who can point a destination somewhere new and then call through it can reach a second system with rights that were never granted to them there, and the trail in the target names the service user rather than the caller.

functions.name: Execute Remote Function / Call Through Destination

risks.name: Develop ABAP and Release the Transport Carrying It
risks.provenance: objects from design spec; field vocabulary UNVERIFIED
risks.rationale: The transport is the control that puts a second pair of eyes between writing code and running it in production. A developer who writes the object AND releases the transport carrying it has removed the only checkpoint in the path, and the release record will show the change as having followed the process. This is the change-management conflict rather than the execution one: what reaches production is decided by the person who wrote it.

risks.name: Import Transports Directly into Production
risks.provenance: objects from design spec (S_TRANSPRT, S_CTS_ADMI); CTS_ADMFCT values not matched by this rule
risks.rationale: The import is the moment code and configuration become real. A user who can import into production can put anything there, including a transport they built themselves or one whose contents were changed after approval, and the import log will record it as a normal promotion. This is the single control that the whole change-management process depends on, and it is frequently granted to whoever is on call.
references: SAP Help - S_TRANSPRT and S_CTS_ADMI transport authorizations
SAP GRC starter ruleset - critical basis access

risks.name: Delete or Reconfigure the Security Audit Log
risks.provenance: object verified (S_ADMI_FCD); this rule does not match on the AUDA/AUDD function values
risks.rationale: Every other control in this report assumes something recorded what happened. The Security Audit Log is that record, and a user who can reconfigure or delete it can decide what the system remembers - switching off a filter before acting and switching it back afterwards, or removing the files outright. Unlike the other critical accesses this one is not primarily about what the holder can do to the business: it is about whether anything would show that they did it, which makes a clean report over an estate holding this access worth less than it appears.

functions.name: Configure or Delete the Security Audit Log

references: SAP Help - Security Audit Log administration (SM18/SM19, RSAU_*)
